Key Activities / Focus: Distribute cluster login credentials, URLs, and troubleshoot immediate network/login friction.

Introduction & Context: What is the tutorial about? (The GFSAD1000 food security narrative).Learning Outcomes: Moving from manual notebooks to automated production architectures.Why Kubeflow?: Overcoming the friction of infrastructure management for data scientists.
Explain the architecture: Ephemeral infrastructure (destroyed post-tutorial), your personal interactive T4 GPU, and the shared 2-GPU batch pool managed by Kueue.
Live instructor walkthrough of the Kubeflow Central Dashboard, provisioning a Notebook Server, and mapping the dataset PVC.
Students provision their own T4 workspace, verify CUDA settings, and evaluate the flawed baseline model.
Discuss the efficiency of cloud-managed GPU workspaces and highlight why the baseline model’s accuracy isn't field-ready.
Instructor shows how manual tweaking fails and walks through creating a Katib Experiment UI/YAML that requests 1-GPU slices from Kueue.
Students launch their Katib HPO experiment, watch Kueue schedule trials 2-at-a-time, and extract the winning parameters.
Highlight how Katib automated the "guessing game" while Kueue fairly distributed trials across the shared cluster resources.
A necessary 10-minute pause for students to stretch, grab coffee, and let any lagging cluster jobs catch up.
Instructor demonstrates taking the winning hyperparameters from Katib and submitting a full-scale, distributed 2-GPU batch job using Kubeflow Trainer.
Students trigger the heavy batch training run, monitor real-time worker logs, and save the optimized production model artifact back to their PVC.
Deep dive into the shift from interactive coding to background batch processing. Point out why we scale up after finding optimal settings.
Instructor explains the fragility of manual scripts and walks through coding Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK components to automate the workflow.
Students wrap data preparation and model paths into Python functions, compile their DAG pipeline, and view the visual execution graph.
Discuss how pipelines act as repeatable production blueprint factories, preparing engineering teams for continuous incoming satellite data.
Instructor demonstrates taking the PVC model artifact and creating a live KServe InferenceService API.
Students deploy their KServe service and send mock HTTP pixel payloads to verify real-time API crop classifications (Irrigated vs. Rainfed).
Review the complete lifecycle: how a model transforms from a static file on a disk into a high-performance web API.
Wrap up the mission narrative, summarize the end-to-end MLOps journey, and distribute the workshop survey link.
